problem: A reopened PowerShell can inherit the Windows Terminal parent's old PATH and fail to locate the installed command.
changes: Derive launcher location from the installing Python profile.
Preserve raw existing user PATH entries and REG_SZ/REG_EXPAND_SZ type.
Install a managed shim only into recognized per-user directories already on the original PATH.
Preserve unknown commands and reject reparse/system-directory alias candidates.
Use direct CMD tail dispatch with literal percent escaping and delayed expansion disabled.
Verify the launcher exists, is discoverable and runs --version before displaying installation success.
Display installation success before opening TUI, and distinguish license verification from installation completion.

cases: PowerShell and CMD newly launched with stale original PATH resolve the managed alias.
Canonical command lookup with a normal Unicode/spaces profile.
Managed shim retains arguments without CALL re-expansion.
windows_path_console.registry_integration_store: in-memory fixture; actual HKCU Environment untouched by tests

path_unit_tests.scope: raw PATH preservation/type, idempotence, canonical names, aliases, conflicts and failure reporting

license_console_regressions.scope: visible key paste, PowerShell onboarding, cancellation, EOF, Python fallback

initial_test_scope_correction.reason: The additional direct canonical PowerShell invocation used a literal environment-variable expression in the directory name. That is a separate legacy CMD dispatch limitation; the stale PATH alias assertions had already succeeded.
initial_test_scope_correction.correction: Keep the difficult percent-containing alias/argument tests and use a separate ordinary Unicode/spaces canonical-path fixture.

limitations: An existing unrelated command is preserved; a shadowing user command may still require manual environment review.
Literal percent-variable expressions in a canonical CMD filename are not universally supported by PowerShell 5 direct invocation; managed-shim dispatch is tested separately.
Custom isolated installs do not persist PATH unless explicitly opted in.
A license-success message alone is not installation completion; wait for the installation-success message.
